chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated from al-Ash'ari, from Samakah ibn Mihran, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Verily, Allah, the Exalted, did not send any Prophet or Imam except that he is the most knowledgeable of the people regarding Allah's affairs, the best of them in appearance, and the most perceptive of them in matters.'

He said: 'And Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, did not make for any of His servants a proof against His servants except through an Imam who calls to Allah, calls to His Messenger, calls to His command, calls to His prohibition, calls to what is halal, calls to what is haram, calls to obedience, and calls to disobedience.'
He said: 'Whoever obeys the Imam has obeyed Allah, and whoever disobeys the Imam has disobeyed Allah.'
ai.seo_question: What are the qualities of an Imam and why is he considered a proof for humanity?
ai.summary: In *Kamal al-Din*, Shaykh al-Saduq uses this hadith to articulate the doctrine of *Ismah* (infallibility) and *Nass* (divine designation), positioning the Imam as the necessary *Hujjah* (proof) who bridges the gap between the Divine and humanity. This establishes the Imam not merely as a political leader but as the living embodiment of divine law, where obedience to him is ontologically linked to obedience to Allah, a concept central to Shia Usuli theology.
